question: Which of these conditions is NOT typically linked to portal hypertension in the liver?

options.A: Dilated submucosal veins
options.B: Bleeding lower vessels
options.C: Oesophageal varices
options.D: Achalasia motility failure

explanation: Spot on! Achalasia is a nerve and muscle issue of the oesophagus itself, completely separate from high blood pressure in the liver circulation.

question: Why do nurses give adjuvant medications along with regular pain relievers?

options.A: They make non-opioids work instantly without side effects
options.B: They help manage specific types of pain like nerve pain
options.C: They prevent the body from ever developing high tolerance
options.D: They completely replace the need for any opioid drugs

explanation: Adjuvants are helper drugs. They tackle tricky types of pain, like shooting nerve pain, that standard painkillers miss.

question: What is the term for giving a patient too many different medications than they actually need?

options.A: Polypharmacy
options.B: Placebo therapy
options.C: Prophylaxis
options.D: Pharmacovigilance

explanation: Good job! Polypharmacy means 'many drugs' and happens when patients take multiple medications at once, increasing the risk of side effects.

question: What does healthcare interoperability allow different computer systems to do?

options.A: Communicate and exchange patient data accurately
options.B: Convert voice recordings into hand-written notes
options.C: Block all external internet traffic for safety
options.D: Automatically print paper prescriptions for patients

explanation: Think of interoperability like a bridge: it simply means different software and hospital gadgets can successfully talk and share information with each other. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which method is commonly used to find out about past exposures in a case-control study?

options.A: Surgical intervention
options.B: Randomized clinical trials
options.C: Direct laboratory observation of future events
options.D: Interviews and questionnaires

explanation: Spot on! Since we are looking backward, we rely heavily on talking to patients and reviewing their past records using questionnaires and interviews.

question: What kind of metabolic shift is typically triggered by major trauma, severe burns, or sepsis?

options.A: Metabolic dormancy
options.B: Hypermetabolic state
options.C: Basal stabilization
options.D: Hypometabolic hibernation

explanation: 'Hyper' means high! Severe physical stress forces the body into overdrive to fight off infection and heal wounds quickly.

question: Which type of white blood cell usually multiplies in the blood during a parasitic or larval invasion?

options.A: Eosinophils
options.B: Erythrocytes
options.C: Basophils
options.D: Platelets

explanation: Your body calls on eosinophils as its special tactical squad to fight off multicellular parasites and worm-like invaders. You've got this nursing concept down!

question: Which level of the Nigerian healthcare system does community health nursing support the most?

options.A: Primary health care
options.B: International health agencies
options.C: Private specialist care
options.D: Tertiary healthcare

explanation: You nailed it! Community health nurses work right at the grassroots level, which is the solid foundation of primary health care in Nigeria.

question: What is a top priority for nursing care right after a laparoscopy?

options.A: Monitoring vital signs and checking for signs of bleeding or pain
options.B: Performing a complete neurological examination of the lower limbs
options.C: Removing surgical stitches before the doctor arrives on the ward
options.D: Discharging the patient home without waiting for full recovery

explanation: Spot on! Right after surgery, keeping an eye on vital signs and watching for bleeding or heavy pain keeps our patient safe.

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Health Record (EHR) in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: To automatically prescribe medications without a doctor's order
options.B: To track the daily attendance and payroll of hospital staff
options.C: To store a comprehensive digital history of a patient's health information
options.D: To manage the public financial budget of the hospital

explanation: Correct! An EHR keeps all of a patient's medical history, test results, and treatments in one digital folder so authorized health workers can see them easily.

question: A nurse checks a patient's skin, hair, and oral mucosa for signs of vitamin deficiencies. Which part of the ABCD framework is this?

options.A: Dietary history
options.B: Anthropometric measurements
options.C: Clinical examination
options.D: Biochemical data

explanation: Looking directly at physical features like hair texture and mucous membranes falls under the clinical examination category. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h2)

question: Why is it dangerous when communities keep quiet about adolescent sexual health?

options.A: It permanently stops physical growth and puberty changes
options.B: It encourages adolescents to seek out professional clinic advice early
options.C: It forces teenagers to rely on misinformed peers for guidance
options.D: It eliminates all forms of peer pressure in secondary schools

explanation: Spot on. When adults refuse to talk about these topics, teens don't stop wondering—they just ask their friends instead, leading to myths and risky choices.

question: What is the main goal of psychological first aid (PFA) when used by nurses in an IDP camp?

options.A: To prescribe strong sedative medications for insomnia
options.B: To cure long-standing clinical schizophrenia permanently
options.C: To diagnose underlying personality disorders in adults
options.D: To offer humane, supportive comfort and reduce immediate distress

explanation: PFA is about listening, offering practical care, and comforting people without forcing them to relive traumatic events.

question: What should a cataract surgery patient wear while sleeping during early recovery?

options.A: A rigid protective eye shield
options.B: A dark pair of polarized sunglasses
options.C: A sterile moist gauze dressing
options.D: A tight elastic pressure bandage

explanation: Wearing a hard shield to bed ensures the patient doesn't accidentally rub or press on their healing eye while fast asleep.

question: In the standard metric BMI formula, how is height measured?

options.A: Inches
options.B: Centimeters
options.C: Meters squared
options.D: Millimeters

explanation: The standard metric formula needs height in meters, which you then square. You've got this!

question: What is the big difference between a totally blame-free environment and a 'Just Culture'?

options.A: A blame-free environment punishes all errors severely
options.B: A blame-free environment requires police involvement for slips
options.C: A Just Culture ignores minor mistakes made by doctors
options.D: A Just Culture still holds workers accountable for reckless actions

explanation: Remember, 'Just Culture' isn't a free-for-all. We forgive honest human slips, but we draw a hard line against dangerous, reckless shortcuts.

question: Which contraceptive option is a long-acting reversible method placed right inside the uterus?

options.A: Combined oral pill
options.B: Emergency contraceptive pill
options.C: Spermicidal foam
options.D: Intrauterine device

explanation: An IUD is a fantastic, worry-free option that sits quietly inside the uterus for years, providing continuous protection that you can stop anytime.

question: What is a main goal of encouraging self-management in home care?

options.A: Reducing the number of home visits a nurse must make
options.B: Ensuring the family takes over all medical tasks permanently
options.C: Lowering the cost of prescription medications for the client
options.D: Helping clients maintain control over their daily activities

explanation: Well done! Empowering clients means they stay independent and confident in managing their own daily routines.

question: Which of these is a key responsibility for a nurse working in public health cancer advocacy?

options.A: Organizing community awareness and teaching early detection methods
options.B: Diagnosing cancer stages without the need for pathology reports
options.C: Performing independent surgical removal of malignant tumors
options.D: Manufacturing chemotherapy medications in hospital pharmacies

explanation: Brilliant! Nurses play a leading role in public health by educating communities, spreading awareness, and encouraging early screening.

question: What is the primary purpose of inflammation in the human body?

options.A: To decrease blood flow to injured areas
options.B: To permanently increase the body temperature
options.C: To speed up the breakdown of red blood cells
options.D: To destroy foreign invaders and repair damaged tissue

explanation: The immune system initiates inflammation specifically to neutralize threats and heal injuries. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h1)

question: A patient with a new leg cast complains of severe, throbbing pain that pain meds aren't helping. What is your first step?

options.A: Apply a heating pad over the cast to relax the cramped calf muscles
options.B: Administer a stronger dose of narcotic pain medication immediately
options.C: Elevate the leg above heart level and wait another two hours to see
options.D: Perform a neurovascular assessment of the toes and check for cast tightness

explanation: Unrelieved pain is a big red flag for dangerous swelling! Always check circulation, motion, and sensation (neurovascular check) right away.

question: What term describes paralysis that affects both legs and the lower half of the body?

options.A: Hemiplegia
options.B: Autonomia
options.C: Tetraplegia
options.D: Paraplegia

explanation: You're doing amazing! Paraplegia means loss of movement and feeling in the lower half of the body, usually happening when there is damage to the mid or lower back (thoracic or lumbar spine).

question: Where does the federal VAPP Act automatically apply right after being signed?

options.A: Lagos State only
options.B: All thirty-six states simultaneously
options.C: Rural communities only
options.D: Federal Capital Territory, Abuja

explanation: Correct! The federal VAPP Act applies directly in the FCT. For other states, their local houses of assembly have to 'domesticate' it first.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to effective delegation by a nurse manager?

options.A: Having too many adequately trained staff members available
options.B: Lack of clear job descriptions and rigid hospital rules
options.C: Fear that subordinates might perform tasks better
options.D: Reluctance to let go of control due to perfectionism

explanation: Having a well-trained team actually makes delegation easier, not harder! The other options are classic roadblocks for managers learning to let go.

question: How can a learning disability affect other children in the family?

options.A: Siblings may experience feelings of neglect or added stress
options.B: Siblings automatically develop the exact same learning disability
options.C: Siblings lose all of their academic abilities
options.D: Siblings are completely unaffected by the situation

explanation: Family dynamics shift when one child requires extensive attention and advocacy, which can impact brothers and sisters emotionally. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h7)

question: According to Maslow, what must be met before anyone can focus on higher-level needs like self-esteem?

options.A: Peer recognition and leadership roles
options.B: Basic physiological and safety needs
options.C: Advanced professional certifications
options.D: Long-term retirement investment goals

explanation: Think of it like building a house: you need a solid foundation of food, water, and safety before you can worry about chasing big personal goals.

question: A nurse tries to explain a complex drug schedule to a patient in a crowded, noisy emergency hallway. What barrier is most likely getting in the way?

options.A: Excessive time available for detailed discussion
options.B: Complete absence of any clinical staff presence
options.C: Environmental distractions and lack of privacy
options.D: The patient's advanced knowledge of pharmacology

explanation: Busy hospital hallways are loud and chaotic, making it super hard for anyone to concentrate on important health advice.

question: What is the main purpose of a home visit in community nursing?

options.A: To perform major surgical procedures at home
options.B: To assess the financial status of the family
options.C: To provide care in the patient's natural environment
options.D: To replace hospital admission completely

explanation: Home visits bring healthcare directly to where patients live so nurses can see their everyday environment and support them there. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h1)

question: How did the post-WWII era change the main reason why nursing homes were opened?

options.A: Religious organizations closed all facilities to focus solely on home nursing
options.B: Communities stopped caring for older adults outside of acute hospitals
options.C: Governments took direct control of all private health institutions
options.D: Eldercare shifted from a charitable or public welfare function into a commercial business

explanation: With hospitals discharging more chronically ill older adults, private business owners saw a chance to step in and turn eldercare into a profitable commercial venture.

question: What is the primary goal of health care waste management?

options.A: To prevent infection and environmental harm
options.B: To create extra work for nursing staff
options.C: To reduce hospital running costs
options.D: To clear up floor space in wards

explanation: Managing medical waste safely stops the spread of disease and protects both hospital workers and the outside community from dangerous materials. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h1)

question: When does prenatal screening for home delivery suitability begin?

options.A: Only when labor pains start
options.B: At the very first antenatal booking visit
options.C: During the third trimester only
options.D: After the baby is born

explanation: Screening must start early during the first antenatal visit to establish baseline health and identify risk factors immediately. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h5)

question: What digital security feature makes sure hospital staff can only open patient files that match their specific job duties?

options.A: Role-based access controls
options.B: Bar code patient wristbands
options.C: Automated audit trails
options.D: Clinical decision support

explanation: Spot on! Role-based access makes sure you only see what you need for your clinical duties—keeping patient privacy locked down tight.

question: A nurse always volunteers to plan ward parties and loves keeping everyone happy together. Which need is this nurse showing?

options.A: Need for achievement
options.B: Need for physiological rest
options.C: Need for personal power
options.D: Need for affiliation

explanation: That's right! Affiliation is all about building warm friendships, belonging to a group, and keeping harmony.

question: Which imaging tool is considered the gold standard for mapping complex reproductive tract birth defects?

options.A: MRI
options.B: X-ray
options.C: Urinalysis
options.D: Wet mount

explanation: Correct! Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) gives super clear pictures of soft tissues, making it the best choice for planning surgery on complex malformations.

question: Which nutrient is especially important early in pregnancy to help prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Sodium chloride
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Potassium

explanation: Correct! Folic acid is a hero in early pregnancy because it helps the baby's brain and spinal cord form properly.

question: Why is buying healthcare different from buying regular items like shoes or phones?

options.A: The price of medical care never changes based on economic factors
options.B: Patients can easily treat themselves without professional assistance
options.C: Healthcare items are always distributed by governments for free
options.D: People demand healthcare because they want health, not because it is a source of pleasure

explanation: Nobody wakes up wishing to visit the hospital for fun! We seek care simply to get our health back and function well. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which vaccines should nurses recommend to help protect patients against viral STIs and related long-term complications?

options.A: Tetanus and diphtheria
options.B: BCG and yellow fever
options.C: HPV and Hepatitis B
options.D: Malaria and typhoid

explanation: Spot on! HPV and Hep B vaccines are powerful shields against major viral infections that can cause serious long-term issues like liver damage or cancers.

question: Why might a standard keyword search miss relevant articles that a MeSH search would easily find?

options.A: MeSH databases hide articles that were published before 1990
options.B: Authors use different words for the same clinical condition
options.C: Standard keywords are illegal to use in evidence-based practice
options.D: Computers cannot read lowercase letters in standard search bars

explanation: If an author uses 'heart attack' instead of 'myocardial infarction', a strict keyword search might miss it, whereas a MeSH term covers both. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which set of clinical signs points straight to hypothyroidism?

options.A: Weight loss, heat intolerance, and rapid pulse
options.B: Severe hypertension, sweating, and tremors
options.C: Extreme thirst, frequent urination, and high sugar
options.D: Weight gain, cold intolerance, and sluggishness

explanation: When thyroid hormones drop, your body's engine slows way down. You feel cold, tired, and your metabolism drops, leading to weight gain.

question: A woman who took oral medications for Type 2 diabetes for five years becomes pregnant. How is her condition classified?

options.A: Transient pregnancy hyperglycemia
options.B: Pregestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Secondary placental diabetes

explanation: Because she had diagnosed diabetes and took medications before getting pregnant, her condition is classified as pregestational diabetes. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h2)

question: What does a glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) test actually tell us about a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Average blood glucose control over the past two to three months
options.B: The exact blood sugar level at the exact moment of the blood draw
options.C: The total amount of insulin stored in the pancreatic beta cells
options.D: How quickly the kidneys are filtering sugar out into the urine

explanation: Think of the HbA1c test as a memory log! Because sugar sticks to red blood cells for their 120-day lifespan, this test shows us the big picture of how blood sugar has been managed over the last few months.

question: During a home visit, your patient lets their adult child answer all your medical questions. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Refuse to discuss the care plan until the child leaves the room
options.B: Insist that the client make decisions completely on their own
options.C: Include the child in health education and care planning discussions
options.D: Report the family dynamic as a case of undue financial influence

explanation: Great choice! Respecting family structures means working together with the person they trust to speak for or help them.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of acute salpingitis?

options.A: Swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Sharp pain in the upper right shoulder
options.C: Painless enlargement of the abdomen
options.D: Bilateral lower abdominal pain

explanation: Inflammation of the tubes usually causes lower belly and pelvic pain on both sides.

question: What does a flattening weight curve on a child's growth chart usually mean first?

options.A: Normal physical growth for that specific age
options.B: An early warning sign of a developing problem
options.C: A measurement error by the attending nurse
options.D: A sudden increase in daily physical activity

explanation: Spot on! When the weight line flattens out, it's often the very first clue that nutrition or health is slipping, even before the child looks visibly thin.

question: A rural clinic sees a sudden cluster of Hepatitis C cases all linked to the same treatment room. What does this point to?

options.A: A natural seasonal variation in viral mutations
options.B: A community outbreak driven by unsafe clinical practices
options.C: An airborne respiratory infection spreading through the ward
options.D: A foodborne intoxication from contaminated local water

explanation: When multiple blood-borne infections pop up tied to one facility, it usually points to a breakdown in basic infection control and sterilization. Excellent clinical deduction!

question: You are getting ready to give a bed bath. What is the most important thing to check right before you start?

options.A: Rub thick lotion all over the skin
options.B: Put on sterile gloves right away
options.C: Lock the bed in the highest position
options.D: Test the water temperature for safety

explanation: Always test the water first! Patients might not feel heat well, so checking keeps them safe from accidental burns.

question: What does the term group dynamics refer to in a healthcare setting?

options.A: The official administrative hierarchy of the hospital
options.B: The physical layout of equipment in the clinic ward
options.C: The changing behaviors and interactions within a team
options.D: The total number of patients treated in a single day

explanation: Group dynamics describes how members of a group relate, behave, and influence each other while working toward a goal. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h1)

question: Which Nigerian federal body is primarily responsible for setting national environmental protection laws regarding waste?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Women Affairs
options.B: Standard Organization of Nigeria
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.D: Federal Ministry of Environment

explanation: The Federal Ministry of Environment takes the lead in creating national policies and rules to protect the environment from hazardous waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h1)

question: Which of these actions breaks patient confidentiality?

options.A: Discussing a patient's diagnosis in a hospital cafeteria where visitors are present
options.B: Reviewing lab results for an assigned patient with the attending physician
options.C: Logging out of the workstation computer before leaving the nurses' station
options.D: Accessing the electronic chart of a patient under your direct care

explanation: Never talk about patient details in public spots where visitors or strangers might overhear you!

question: What is a major everyday hurdle for bedside nurses who want to do research?

options.A: Heavy clinical workloads and shift duties
options.B: The absence of any medical terminology in nursing
options.C: Mandatory laws forbidding nurses from collecting data
options.D: A complete lack of patients in government hospitals

explanation: Too true! Juggling busy ward shifts and direct patient care leaves very little breathing room for extra projects.

question: What is the first-choice medication in a midwifery kit to prevent heavy bleeding after birth?

options.A: Amoxicillin
options.B: Diazepam
options.C: Paracetamol
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin is our superstar drug given right after delivery to help the uterus contract and keep postpartum hemorrhage away.

question: An adolescent health clinic welcomes all teenagers regardless of their financial status or background. Which core characteristic is this clinic showing?

options.A: Selective
options.B: Commercial
options.C: Exclusive
options.D: Equitable

explanation: Equitable care simply means fair treatment for every young person, treating everyone with equal care and without any form of discrimination.

question: What is the main purpose of the systemic circulation?

options.A: Filter waste products in the kidneys
options.B: Remove carbon dioxide from the lungs
options.C: Warm up blood before it reaches the brain
options.D: Deliver oxygenated blood to body tissues

explanation: The systemic circuit is responsible for pumping oxygen and nutrients out to all body organs and tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h1)

question: What is the main point of health planning in a community?

options.A: Identifying health problems and using resources to meet goals
options.B: Reducing the total number of patients admitted to wards
options.C: Building more private hospitals in urban centers
options.D: Increasing the salary of medical and nursing personnel

explanation: You've got this! Health planning is simply finding out what health issues a community faces and figuring out how to use available resources to solve them.

question: What is the main job of a standard hearing aid?

options.A: To amplify surrounding sounds so the damaged ear can detect them
options.B: To convert spoken words directly into written text on a screen
options.C: To remove impacted earwax from deep inside the ear canal
options.D: To surgically replace the cochlea with an electronic processor

explanation: Exactly! Think of a hearing aid as a tiny personal amplifier that makes everyday sounds loud enough for the ear to pick up.

question: A patient's forehead temperature reads 37.8°C, but they look pale and are shivering hard. What should you suspect?

options.A: The patient has a severe brain injury
options.B: Shivering can make skin feel cold while a real fever is hiding underneath
options.C: The thermometer is definitely broken and should be thrown away
options.D: The patient has no fever at all and needs no more checks

explanation: When shivering causes surface blood vessels to tighten up, skin readings can look normal or low even when core temperature is climbing. Always keep a close eye!

question: Where is the correct spot to inject an emergency epinephrine auto-injector?

options.A: The soft skin directly over the abdomen
options.B: The upper fatty tissue of the arm
options.C: The large muscle of the buttocks
options.D: The outer middle thigh muscle

explanation: Spot on! The outer middle thigh (anterolateral thigh) has great muscle and blood flow for the fastest drug absorption during an emergency.

question: Why do many psychiatric patients try alternative healing methods?

options.A: To reduce medication side effects and gain personal control
options.B: To avoid speaking with healthcare providers entirely
options.C: To increase the cost of their psychiatric treatment
options.D: To completely replace all forms of medical documentation

explanation: Patients often explore natural or alternative therapies to feel better while avoiding harsh drug side effects, and it helps them feel more involved in their own recovery!

question: How do patients with illness anxiety disorder usually react to normal, everyday body sensations like a slight muscle twitch?

options.A: They report them exclusively to family members only
options.B: They ignore them completely as routine physiology
options.C: They misinterpret them as signs of catastrophic disease
options.D: They use them to plan healthy physical exercise routines

explanation: Think of it this way: a normal minor ache gets blown completely out of proportion, making the patient convinced it's a hidden, dangerous sickness.

question: Why does the Model for Improvement focus on small tests of change rather than massive overhauls?

options.A: Hospital management bans large projects due to budget constraints
options.B: Small tests reduce risk and let staff see if a change works before spreading it
options.C: Regulatory bodies only permit one minor change per year
options.D: Patients refuse to participate in large-scale hospital studies

explanation: Spot on! Testing things on a small scale lets nurses safely try out new ideas without disrupting the whole ward.

question: While in a helicopter, your intubated patient suddenly becomes restless and starts breathing very fast. What should you check first?

options.A: The exact mileage remaining until the destination
options.B: Airway security and oxygen saturation levels
options.C: The patient's personal identification documents
options.D: Whether family members signed the consent forms

explanation: Sudden restlessness and fast breathing usually mean the patient isn't getting enough oxygen. Always check the airway and oxygen levels immediately!

question: Why are pure opioid agonists like morphine considered strong pain relievers?

options.A: They fully activate mu receptors to stop severe pain signals.
options.B: They never cause any unwanted side effects in the body.
options.C: They eliminate all inflammation directly at the injury site.
options.D: They only work on mild headaches and minor muscle sprains.

explanation: Morphine locks strongly onto mu receptors in the central nervous system, which is why it's so powerful at knocking out severe pain.

question: What does a pulse oximeter actually measure in the patient?

options.A: Exact blood pressure inside the artery
options.B: Total red blood cell count in the body
options.C: Oxygen saturation percentage in the blood
options.D: Carbon dioxide levels in the lungs

explanation: The device uses light absorption to estimate how much hemoglobin is carrying oxygen. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h2)

question: You notice a patient's GCS score dropped from 14 to 10 over two hours. What should you do right away?

options.A: Document the score in the chart and leave the room for a break.
options.B: Administer a strong sleeping pill to calm the restless patient.
options.C: Wait another four hours to see if the patient wakes up naturally.
options.D: Notify the healthcare provider immediately and report the neurological decline.

explanation: A dropping GCS score is an urgent red flag! Any sudden decline in a patient's alertness means you must alert the doctor right away.

question: What is a great way to keep a multisectoral team accountable and working well together?

options.A: Holding meetings only once every five years to review old records
options.B: Leaving each sector to work completely independently without reporting back
options.C: Establishing joint monitoring committees with representatives from all involved sectors
options.D: Allowing the health ministry to make all decisions without consulting others

explanation: Correct! Joint committees help everyone stay on the same page, track shared goals, and solve problems as a team.

question: A nurse notices that teenage patients look nervous and hesitant when entering the consultation room. What immediate action should the nurse take?

options.A: Refuse to examine the patient until an older family member arrives
options.B: Scold the teenager for being afraid of a routine medical checkup
options.C: Use a warm tone and a welcoming posture to help put the teen at ease
options.D: Insist that a security guard stays inside the room during the interview

explanation: A welcoming attitude and friendly demeanor help break down anxiety and build trust with young clients. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h6)

question: You are teaching a community group how to prevent lifestyle diseases like diabetes and high blood pressure. What is the best advice to give?

options.A: Educating them on eating balanced meals with proper nutrient proportions
options.B: Advising them to completely eliminate all forms of dietary fat
options.C: Suggesting they rely entirely on vitamin pills instead of fresh food
options.D: Encouraging them to drink less than two glasses of water daily

explanation: Balance is key! Teaching communities to eat a variety of properly proportioned, wholesome meals is the best way to prevent diet-related illnesses.

question: What is the main feature of an ergonomic workplace injury?

options.A: It results only from extreme cold temperatures
options.B: It develops slowly over time from repeated physical strain
options.C: It is caused by breathing in airborne bacteria
options.D: It happens instantly from an explosion or spill

explanation: Ergonomic injuries like carpal tunnel or back strain build up gradually when our bodies are subjected to poor posture and repetitive movements.

question: What is the main purpose of reflective practice in nursing?

options.A: To punish staff members who make clinical mistakes
options.B: To turn everyday experience into professional growth
options.C: To replace the formal nursing assessment process
options.D: To reduce the paperwork required at shift handover

explanation: Reflective practice allows nurses to learn from past situations and improve future care. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h6)

question: A patient is confused about taking multiple pills at different times of the day. What is the most practical nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to stop taking all medications until the doctor visits
options.B: Ask the family pharmacist to move all drugs into liquid formulations
options.C: Instruct the client to take all daily pills together every morning
options.D: Set up a labeled weekly pill organizer with the patient or family

explanation: Well done! A weekly pill box is a simple, practical lifesaver. It cuts down confusion and helps patients take the right meds at the right time.

question: Which sampling method involves picking every 5th or 10th person from an organized list?

options.A: Systematic sampling
options.B: Simple random sampling
options.C: Stratified sampling
options.D: Convenience sampling

explanation: Brilliant! Systematic sampling means you use a fixed math interval (like every 10th nurse on the roster) after a random start.

question: Around how many weeks of pregnancy do morning sickness and nausea usually start?

options.A: 1 to 3 weeks
options.B: 16 to 18 weeks
options.C: 10 to 12 weeks
options.D: 4 to 6 weeks

explanation: You will often see this early in the first trimester around weeks 4 to 6, right when hormones start shooting up. Great job keeping this in mind for antenatal care!

question: A nurse starts a support group for people living with sickle cell across the entire state. What type of community is this?

options.A: Geopolitical community
options.B: Municipal community
options.C: Phenomenological community
options.D: Structural community

explanation: You're getting it! When people are united by a shared experience or health condition rather than just living on the same street, it's a phenomenological community.

question: Why do researchers often prefer the median over the mean when looking at how long patients stay in the hospital?

options.A: The median is much harder to calculate using modern computer software
options.B: Length of stay can only be measured in whole numbers of days
options.C: A few patients staying an unusually long time can distort the average
options.D: Hospital administrators refuse to look at mathematical averages

explanation: Extreme outliers, like a patient staying 100 days, pull the mean way up, whereas the median stays stable and shows the typical experience.

question: Which group is generally at the highest risk of abuse and neglect in home care settings?

options.A: Young adults recovering from minor sports injuries
options.B: Physically independent middle-aged business executives
options.C: Healthcare professionals working in community clinics
options.D: Frail elderly individuals and those with memory issues

explanation: Spot on! People who are physically frail or have cognitive challenges often depend heavily on others, making them more vulnerable to mistreatment.

question: Which ethical principle guides a nurse's duty to act in the best interest of their psychiatric patient?

options.A: Veracity
options.B: Beneficence
options.C: Paternalism
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Beneficence is all about doing good and taking positive actions to care for and protect your patients. It's at the heart of nursing ethics!

question: A patient just had cataract surgery and is getting ready to go home. What is a key instruction to give them?

options.A: Wash your face vigorously with antibacterial soap daily
options.B: Sleep flat on your back without using any pillows
options.C: Avoid heavy lifting and straining during bowel movements
options.D: Keep the affected eye uncovered at all times

explanation: Spot on! Straining or heavy lifting ramps up the pressure inside the eye, which is the last thing you want right after eye surgery.

question: What does self-medication mean in everyday terms?

options.A: Participating in a clinical drug trial supervised by researchers
options.B: Using medicines to treat self-recognized symptoms without a prescription
options.C: Receiving intravenous medications exclusively inside a hospital ward
options.D: Taking drugs strictly prescribed and monitored by a licensed physician

explanation: Self-medication simply means buying or taking drugs on your own to treat symptoms without getting a doctor's go-ahead first. You've got this!

question: Which nursing action is unsafe for a patient at high risk of bleeding?

options.A: Brushing teeth with a soft sponge
options.B: Using a sliding board for transfers
options.C: Checking urine output every shift
options.D: Taking a routine rectal temperature

explanation: Rectal thermometers can easily scratch the delicate lining down there and trigger bleeding. Always choose a safer route!

question: What is the main danger when handling genotoxic healthcare waste, such as cancer chemotherapy drugs?

options.A: Sudden acute bacterial infections
options.B: Severe electrolyte imbalance
options.C: Damage to cellular DNA and cancer risk
options.D: Immediate thermal skin burns

explanation: Genotoxic means 'toxic to genes.' These powerful drugs mess with cell DNA, which can cause mutations or cancer over time if we don't handle them with strict care.

question: Which of these is considered a redundancy error in research writing?

options.A: Including a table number at the top of the grid
options.B: Writing out every single number from a table inside the narrative text
options.C: Using the same font style for all headings in the paper
options.D: Placing explanatory footnotes below the table body

explanation: Listing every single table number word-for-word in your text is repetitive. Your text should just highlight the main trends instead!

question: What is the primary goal of social services for persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: Eliminating all physical impairments completely
options.B: Providing permanent institutional care for everyone
options.C: Promoting independence and equal participation
options.D: Replacing the need for medical rehabilitation

explanation: Social services focus on empowering individuals to live as independently as possible and take part in society on an equal basis with others. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h1)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to chat about a patient's daily routine before choosing a birth control method?

options.A: To match the patient with a method they can use consistently
options.B: To test the patient's ability to read complex medical textbooks
options.C: To calculate the exact financial tax for purchasing the drugs
options.D: To determine if the patient has any hidden genetic disorders

explanation: Great nursing care is personalized! Knowing a patient's lifestyle helps you suggest a method—like a daily pill versus a 3-year implant—that genuinely fits their everyday life.

question: What should you do if you notice a colleague accidentally contaminate a sterile setup during a procedure?

options.A: Carry on if the patient looks okay and feels fine
options.B: Blame the patient for moving around on the bed
options.C: Wait until the procedure is over to tell them in private
options.D: Stop right away and get new, clean sterile items

explanation: Safety first, always! Patient protection comes before anything else, so we pause immediately to fix a break in technique.

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention programs in substance abuse control?

options.A: Stopping individuals from ever experimenting with harmful drugs in the first place
options.B: Helping long-term recovering addicts find stable employment after treatment
options.C: Imposing strict criminal prison sentences on local drug traffickers
options.D: Providing immediate emergency detox in a specialized intensive care unit

explanation: Primary prevention is all about stopping the issue before it starts by educating healthy populations. Prevention is always better than cure!

question: When writing a research proposal for a study you haven't done yet, what tense should you use?

options.A: Future tense
options.B: Conditional tense
options.C: Present tense
options.D: Past tense

explanation: Since the research hasn't happened yet, you're planning for what you *will* do. That means keeping everything in the future tense!

question: What kind of food is best to suggest for a patient suffering from painful mouth ulcers?

options.A: Hot, spicy, and crunchy snacks
options.B: Dry, salty crackers and toast
options.C: Acidic citrus fruits and juices
options.D: Cool, bland, and soft foods

explanation: Cool, soft, and gentle foods help keep the patient comfortable and avoid irritating sensitive sores.

question: What is a major nursing concern when an older adult has severe dental problems and missing teeth?

options.A: Increased likelihood of developing hypertension
options.B: Rapid cognitive decline within forty-eight hours
options.C: Immediate kidney failure due to poor digestion
options.D: Risk of malnutrition and difficulty chewing certain foods

explanation: When chewing hurts or is difficult, residents might skip healthy foods like meat and raw veggies unless their meals are specially prepared. You are learning great clinical foresight!

question: Why do we apply a cold pack to a mum's perineum during the first 24 hours after a vaginal delivery?

options.A: To speed up uterine involution
options.B: To stimulate lochia production
options.C: To reduce swelling and numb pain
options.D: To prevent milk engorgement

explanation: You nailed it! Cold packs narrow the local blood vessels, which keeps swelling down and gives the sore perineal area a nice numbing relief.

question: Which group of professionals is most ideal for creating a complete care plan for a special needs child?

options.A: Only traditional spiritual healers
options.B: A multidisciplinary team including nurses, therapists, and social workers
options.C: Only hospital accountants and security guards
options.D: Exclusive teams of pharmaceutical sales reps

explanation: Special needs touch on health, education, and social life, so working together in a multidisciplinary team gives the child the best possible holistic care.

question: How do local farmers directly support school feeding initiatives?

options.A: By teaching science classes on agricultural botany
options.B: By prescribing nutritional supplements to sick children
options.C: By supplying locally grown, nutritious food produce
options.D: By auditing the financial books of the school canteen

explanation: Local farmers provide fresh food ingredients, ensuring the feeding program is sustainable and utilizes local produce. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the medical definition of a fracture?

options.A: A stretching injury to the ligaments surrounding a joint
options.B: A complete break or crack in the continuity of a bone
options.C: An infection located deep inside the bone marrow
options.D: A sudden tear in the muscle fibers attached to bone

explanation: A fracture simply means the physical structure of the bone has cracked or broken due to stress or trauma. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why is maintaining strict confidentiality regarding family planning crucial in community nursing?

options.A: To prevent the clinic from keeping accurate statistical records
options.B: To ensure that contraceptives are sold at higher market prices
options.C: To protect clients from social stigma and domestic conflict
options.D: To hide the nurse's activities from local government leaders

explanation: Clients may face backlash or relationship issues if their contraceptive choices are shared without permission in tight-knit communities. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h8)

question: What does Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) actually measure?

options.A: The total calories burned during heavy physical exercise
options.B: The energy needed to maintain basic life functions at rest
options.C: The amount of heat produced during food digestion
options.D: The maximum oxygen consumption during endurance training

explanation: Think of BMR as your body's idle speed. It's the bare minimum energy required to keep your heart pumping, lungs breathing, and organs working while you do absolutely nothing.

question: Why must nurses check for G6PD deficiency before giving a patient primaquine?

options.A: To prevent severe hemolytic anemia in vulnerable patients
options.B: To confirm the liver is strong enough to process the drug
options.C: To ensure the patient does not have a concurrent bacterial infection
options.D: To check if the patient is already immune to malaria

explanation: Safety first! Patients with G6PD deficiency lack the protection needed to keep their red blood cells stable against primaquine, which can trigger dangerous red blood cell breakdown (hemolysis).

question: What does the 'drop factor' on an IV tubing package tell you?

options.A: The number of drops delivered in one milliliter of fluid
options.B: The maximum speed the fluid can flow through the line
options.C: The total number of milliliters the tubing can hold
options.D: The hours the administration set can remain sterile

explanation: You've got this. Drop factor tells you the size of the drops the tubing makes, which you need to know when calculating manual drip rates (gtt/min).

question: How does a soft diet differ from a pureed diet?

options.A: Soft diets are strictly liquid-based
options.B: Pureed diets require more chewing effort than soft diets
options.C: Soft diets contain recognizable food pieces requiring minimal chewing
options.D: Pureed diets allow raw vegetables and nuts

explanation: While pureed diets blend everything into a smooth paste, soft diets still feature actual pieces of food that are simply tender and easy to mash. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h1)

question: Why is keeping enough potassium inside the cells so crucial for your patients?

options.A: It directly controls blood pressure in the arteries
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from producing too much urine
options.C: It regulates red blood cell production in bone marrow
options.D: It maintains stable heart rhythm and muscle action

explanation: Exactly! Potassium is a heart-loving electrolyte. When potassium levels go out of whack, the heart and muscles can struggle to beat properly.

question: What do the four letters in the PDSA quality improvement cycle stand for?

options.A: Plan, Do, Study, Act
options.B: Prepare, Design, Streamline, Assess
options.C: Predict, Document, Sort, Analyze
options.D: Practice, Direct, Secure, Apply

explanation: PDSA is a handy little cycle we use to test changes: Plan your test, Do it, Study the results, and Act on what you learned!

question: Which physical check is a reliable sign of dehydration, especially in older adults?

options.A: Increased muscle tone in the upper arms
options.B: Dry mucous membranes inside the mouth
options.C: Cool skin temperature in the lower legs
options.D: Reduced skin turgor on the back of the hand

explanation: Skin turgor can be tricky in older adults due to aging skin, but checking inside the mouth for moisture is very reliable.

question: Which tool is most commonly used for rapid neurological assessment in emergency settings?

options.A: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.B: Comprehensive mental status questionnaire
options.C: Deep tendon reflex chart
options.D: Full cranial nerve checklist

explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale provides a quick, reliable score for eye, verbal, and motor responses during emergencies. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h7)

question: In which year did the World Health Organization publish its first model list of essential medicines?
explanation: The World Health Organization introduced the very first model list in 1977 to help countries prioritize public health needs. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: A patient calls three days after her polypectomy reporting mild lower belly cramps and very light pink spotting. What should the nurse say?

options.A: Schedule an emergency surgical re-exploration
options.B: Advise her to start taking oral antibiotics right away
options.C: Instruct her to report immediately to the emergency room
options.D: Reassure her that this is a normal, expected finding

explanation: A little bit of cramping and light spotting is totally normal after the cervix has been touched or treated. Just reassure and comfort her!

question: What is the main function of neuroglia cells in the nervous system?

options.A: To release hormones straight into the bloodstream
options.B: To support, protect, and nourish neurons
options.C: To generate electrical impulses for muscle movement
options.D: To carry signals directly from the skin to the brain

explanation: Neuroglia do not send nerve signals themselves; instead, they act as support staff that protect and feed the active neurons. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h1)

question: A patient recovering from a severe stroke struggles to walk and needs help rebuilding muscle strength. Which team member should be consulted?

options.A: Physician
options.B: Physiotherapist
options.C: Pharmacist
options.D: Social worker

explanation: You nailed it! Physiotherapists are experts at helping patients regain movement, strength, and independence after major setbacks like strokes.

question: Why does a lack of basic education often lead to higher rates of unintended pregnancies?

options.A: It guarantees employment in high-stress urban environments
options.B: It increases the biological fertility rate of every woman
options.C: It physically alters the organs of the reproductive system
options.D: It limits access to accurate information on how to prevent conception

explanation: Exactly! Without proper education, people are left relying on myths instead of solid facts about family planning.

question: How do daily community health records help with national health planning in Nigeria?

options.A: They provide data on actual community consumption to help distribute supplies
options.B: They replace the need to conduct national population censuses
options.C: They automatically set the market prices for essential drugs
options.D: They prove to foreign donors that nurses are working hard every day

explanation: Great job thinking big picture! Records from local clinics show ministries how many vaccines and drugs are actually used, helping them send more supplies where needed.

question: Why is recording the exact date and vaccine type so important for community health?

options.A: It proves to patients that the nurse has good handwriting
options.B: It allows the clinic to calculate daily financial profits
options.C: It prevents missed appointments and avoids duplicate dosing
options.D: It stops vaccine manufacturers from making more doses

explanation: Good records help us track when the next dose is due and make sure patients don't get accidental double doses.

question: Why would a nurse researcher use a Chi-Square test?

options.A: To calculate the average dosage response of a new drug
options.B: To measure the exact mean difference between two groups
options.C: To predict future patient mortality rates using time curves
options.D: To see if two categorical variables are related

explanation: Great thinking! We use it to check if two category-based things are connected—for example, seeing if a patient's ward location is linked to getting an infection.

question: A family caring for a child with cerebral palsy is struggling to afford mobility aids and therapy sessions. What kind of support should you recommend?

options.A: Financial assistance and rehabilitation services
options.B: Commercial banking loans
options.C: Adult vocational training centers
options.D: Tax exemption advisory boards

explanation: Welfare grants and rehabilitation therapy are designed to directly help families manage the financial and physical demands of special needs care.

question: What is the main goal of disease control in public health?

options.A: Treating individual patients at the bedside
options.B: Eliminating the need for primary healthcare centers
options.C: Reducing transmission and illness in a population
options.D: Managing hospital budgets and administrative staff

explanation: Spot on! While bedside nursing focuses on one patient at a time, public health looks at the big picture to protect entire communities from getting sick.

question: What is the main goal of using the nursing process in everyday clinical practice?

options.A: To replace the need for direct communication with physicians
options.B: To fulfill mandatory hospital paperwork requirements only
options.C: To determine the financial cost of hospital stays
options.D: To provide a clear, step-by-step guide for giving personal patient care

explanation: Think of the nursing process as your trusty roadmap! It helps you organize your thoughts and actions so you can safely meet each patient's unique health needs.

question: In research language, what is a 'sampling frame'?

options.A: A framework for writing up the final research report
options.B: The physical room where patient interviews take place
options.C: A complete list of everyone in the accessible population
options.D: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size

explanation: Think of a sampling frame as your phone book or registry list. It's the actual directory of names you draw your participants from!

question: In which operating theatre zone must staff always wear a surgical mask over their nose and mouth?

options.A: Unrestricted zone
options.B: Semi-restricted zone
options.C: Administrative zone
options.D: Restricted zone

explanation: Masks are a must in the restricted zone, where open wounds and sterile trays are exposed to the environment.

question: How full can a sharps box get before you must close and replace it?

options.A: One-quarter full
options.B: Completely packed to the top rim
options.C: Whenever it starts smelling bad
options.D: Three-quarters full

explanation: Safety first! Always seal and replace sharps containers when they are three-quarters full so needles don't poke out and accidentally injure someone.

question: Serum sickness is a classic example of which type of hypersensitivity reaction?

options.A: Type I hypersensitivity
options.B: Type II hypersensitivity
options.C: Type IV hypersensitivity
options.D: Type III hypersensitivity

explanation: You've got this! Serum sickness is a type III reaction that happens when immune complexes build up in the body.

question: How should a nurse manager respond to an employee who engages in at-risk behavior, such as taking a minor shortcut because of heavy workload?

options.A: Ignore the action completely as long as no one died.
options.B: Fire the nurse instantly without a hearing.
options.C: Report the nurse to the police for criminal charges.
options.D: Coach the nurse and evaluate the underlying system pressure.

explanation: At-risk behavior involves choices where risk is misunderstood or normalized, so it requires coaching and workflow evaluation rather than harsh punishment. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why are complex blood tests usually not needed to diagnose Guinea worm disease?

options.A: Skin scrapings yield definitive results within minutes
options.B: Blood cell counts remain completely normal throughout the infection
options.C: The parasite is easily visible as it emerges from the skin blister
options.D: The worm releases spores that can be seen with the naked eye

explanation: Spot on! When you can literally see the adult worm poking out of the skin, the diagnosis is clear as day. Brilliant logic!

question: To help prevent Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (VAP), at what angle should the head of the patient's bed be kept?

options.A: 60 to 90 degrees upright
options.B: 30 to 45 degrees
options.C: 15 degrees slightly tilted
options.D: 0 degrees completely flat

question: In young children with sickle cell anaemia, what is dactylitis?

options.A: Severe infection of the lung tissue
options.B: Painful swelling of the hands and feet
options.C: Sudden yellowing of the eyes and skin
options.D: Abnormal enlargement of the liver

explanation: Dactylitis is often one of the very first signs of sickle cell disease in babies. It happens when sickled cells block blood flow in the tiny bones of the hands and feet, causing painful swelling.

question: What is the main reason for running regular hospital disaster drills?

options.A: To completely eliminate the possibility of any future infrastructure damage
options.B: To replace standard daily nursing documentation with emergency charts
options.C: To build team readiness and ensure a smooth emergency response
options.D: To accurately predict the exact calendar date of the next natural disaster

explanation: Practice makes perfect! Drills help staff know their roles inside out, cutting down panic when a real emergency hits.

question: When did the World Health Organization (WHO) publish its first Model List of Essential Medicines?
explanation: Great try! The WHO put out this very first list back in 1977 to bring order, safety, and priority to global drug markets.

question: Why is getting male partners involved in community safe motherhood programs so important in Nigeria?

options.A: They are solely responsible for performing postnatal physical examinations
options.B: They should be excluded from all prenatal health decisions
options.C: They act as primary birth attendants during complicated deliveries
options.D: They control household resources and support decisions to seek timely care

question: A client with advanced dementia who wanders at night is being checked into an assisted living facility that does not have a secure memory unit. What should the facility do?

options.A: Wait until the client's memory improves on its own
options.B: Deny admission because the facility cannot keep the client safe
options.C: Admit the client and just use door chimes for night safety
options.D: Accept the client and assign a private nurse paid by the family

explanation: You've got this! Facilities must match their care to what the client genuinely needs. Admitting a wandering client to an unsecure place creates a big safety risk.

question: What is the main goal of injection safety in healthcare?

options.A: To speed up medication administration processes
options.B: To eliminate the need for personal protective equipment
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing drugs
options.D: To prevent harm to patients, workers, and communities

explanation: Injection safety is all about making sure no one gets hurt—neither the patient getting the shot, the nurse giving it, nor the wider community! You've got this.

question: Which diagnostic imaging tool is best for detecting early bone marrow inflammation and infection?

options.A: Abdominal ultrasound
options.B: Standard chest radiograph
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.D: Electrocardiogram

explanation: MRI provides excellent soft tissue and bone marrow detail, making it the most sensitive imaging method for early-stage osteomyelitis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h6)

question: Why are functional emergency referral systems so important for pregnant women in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policy requires all babies to be born in teaching hospitals
options.B: Patients prefer to pay higher fees at tertiary hospitals rather than local clinics
options.C: Primary health clinics cannot manage severe obstetric emergencies like ruptured uterus or eclampsia
options.D: Primary health centers do not keep any medical records of pregnant women

explanation: Local clinics are great for routine antenatal care, but if a life-threatening emergency like severe eclampsia happens, patients need quick transport to a bigger hospital with a doctor and blood bank.

question: What part of the body does an intravenous pyelography (IVP) mainly check?

options.A: The nervous system
options.B: The urinary system
options.C: The digestive system
options.D: The respiratory system

question: Why does the blood-brain barrier present a major hurdle when treating certain brain infections?

options.A: It actively destroys all types of antibiotics in the blood
options.B: It prevents many helpful medicines from entering brain tissue
options.C: It increases the pressure of cerebrospinal fluid dangerously
options.D: It allows bacteria to hide safely inside the ventricles

explanation: The same tight barriers that keep harmful toxins out also block many beneficial pharmaceutical drugs from reaching infections inside the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h7)

question: A 28-week pregnant patient complains of constant tiredness, slight breathlessness, and a strange craving to chew on dry clay. What's going on?

options.A: Normal physiological changes of late pregnancy
options.B: Pregnancy-induced hypertension with edema
options.C: Severe iron deficiency anaemia with pica
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus with neuropathy

question: Why is a patient during the incubation period often difficult to identify in the community?

options.B: They produce antibodies that instantly neutralize all clinical signs
options.C: They look and feel completely healthy despite harboring the pathogen

question: What is a practical solution for QA committees when computers and digital health records are not available?

options.A: Ignoring clinical data collection entirely
options.B: Using simple, well-designed paper tracking tools and logs
options.C: Stopping all quality checks until computers are donated
options.D: Waiting for patients to remember their own medical histories

explanation: You nailed it! Good paper-based logs keep quality assurance running smoothly even when technology is missing.

question: What is a tracheostomy?

options.A: A tube inserted through the nose into the stomach
options.B: A small incision made in the upper chest wall
options.C: A flexible scope passed down the throat
options.D: A surgical opening made into the trachea

question: What is the main abnormal type of haemoglobin found in sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Haemoglobin S

options.C: Haemoglobin A
options.D: Haemoglobin F

question: Why is getting an autoimmune disease diagnosed often a long and tricky journey?

options.A: Blood tests are completely unavailable for most autoimmune conditions
options.B: Early symptoms are vague, overlapping, and resemble many other common illnesses
options.C: Autoimmune markers change completely every single day
options.D: Patients rarely report their symptoms to healthcare providers early on

explanation: Early signs like tiredness and body aches look like everyday malaria or stress, making it tough for doctors to pin down right away.

question: What is the biggest benefit of bringing mental health care directly into local communities?

options.A: It reduces stigma and improves accessibility to care
options.B: It eliminates the need for any trained medical professionals
options.C: It allows government agencies to stop funding hospitals
options.D: It guarantees that patients will never experience a relapse

explanation: Bringing care closer to home makes it easier for people to get help without feeling the heavy shame or fear attached to traveling to a distant psychiatric hospital.

question: A local health district has a fixed budget to build two new clinics. Based on primary health care principles, where should these clinics be built?

options.A: In affluent neighborhoods where residents can pay user fees
options.B: Inside the capital city near the main teaching hospital
options.C: In the most rural and underserved farming communities
options.D: Next to the regional airport for easy international access

question: Why is the outer one-inch border of a sterile field considered unsterile?

options.A: Because nurses are only allowed to touch the exact center of the tray

options.C: Because the manufacturer marks that area with special invisible ink
options.D: Because it is likely to touch unsterile surfaces during setup and handling

question: Why is a quiet, private environment essential when a nurse conducts a telehealth video call?

options.A: To make the nurse's computer battery last much longer during the shift
options.B: To stop other staff members from asking questions about their work
options.C: To ensure compliance with patient privacy and confidentiality laws
options.D: To prevent background noise from interrupting the internet signal

explanation: Conducting calls in private spaces stops unauthorized people from overhearing sensitive health discussions, protecting patient confidentiality. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which hormone causes the milk ejection reflex (let-down)?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Luteinizing hormone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Correct! Oxytocin is the 'let-down' hormone that makes the milk flow smoothly for your baby.

question: Why don't we use the intraarterial route for everyday medications like regular IVs?

options.A: Intravenous medications are always cheaper to manufacture
options.B: Arteries have no blood flow once a needle enters them
options.C: High arterial pressure makes access and maintenance complex and risky

question: Why do different hospital units need to use consistent terms in patient charts?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will never experience any adverse drug events
options.B: It eliminates the need for nurses to write narrative notes
options.C: It ensures clinical terms and data mean the same thing everywhere
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing electronic health record software

explanation: Consistency means any nurse or doctor reading the notes will understand the findings in the exact same way.

question: What is the main goal of epidemiology in public health?

options.A: Manufacturing vaccines for global distribution
options.B: Managing financial budgets for health clinics
options.C: Treating individual patients in a hospital ward
options.D: Studying how and why diseases spread in a population

explanation: Epidemiology is all about looking at the big picture—how and why health issues affect entire populations, rather than just treating one patient at a time. Great job wrapping your head around this community health fundamental!

question: What waste product does the liver make when processing extra amino acids?

options.A: Lactic acid
options.B: Bile salt
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Urea

explanation: The liver takes toxic ammonia from protein breakdown and turns it into safer urea so your kidneys can easily flush it out.

question: Which chemical is most commonly used for high-level disinfection of heat-sensitive scopes?
